name: Workbench P-005 Windows Papercup resident lifecycle
sourceCustody: Ran against the exact source already measured in workbench-p005-windows-chat-ui-20261108.json before the subsequent cards-core bridge/model edits.

cases: first install enables native panels with distinct default shortcuts

first install enables Inbox on Ctrl Alt B

installer persists the migrated Inbox shortcut
upgrade preserves explicitly disabled Inbox
first install enables Organizer on Ctrl Alt O
Organizer migration avoids existing shortcuts
installer persists the migrated Organizer shortcut
upgrade preserves explicitly disabled Organizer
Organizer upgrade retains the prior Quick Access shortcut
first install enables Papercup on Ctrl Alt P
Papercup migration avoids existing shortcuts

upgrade preserves explicitly disabled Papercup
Papercup upgrade retains existing surface preferences
adding Accounts preserves legacy disable and shortcut choices

preserve-existing installer persists the missing Accounts binding
login registration uses the exact installed controller and fixed argv
Workbench registration preserves unrelated login applications
native login command preserves spaces apostrophes and literal dollar signs
upgrade preserves account shortcuts and individual panel disable
upgrade refreshes the registered installation without resetting choices
disable removes this accounts Workbench login value
reinstall does not re-enable an explicitly disabled account
explicit enable restores login registration
duplicate enabled shortcuts are refused before writing
reserved F12 remains invalid even for a disabled panel
invalid native modifier bits are refused
invalid settings leave both persistence and login state unchanged
concurrent settings writer cannot bypass the per-account lock
registry failure is surfaced instead of accepting a partial settings update
registry failure restores the previous settings
missing resident is reported without starting a service or touching another account
settings wake targets the exact account and state-directory identity

uninstall removes owned login registration and retains account preferences
retained preferences survive uninstall and reinstall
corrupt preferences fail visibly instead of silently resetting shortcuts

actual controller starts the resident in the signed-in desktop and acknowledges native readiness

native settings persist explicit disable
login invocation respects the saved disabled choice
explicit enable restarts the same configured native host
explicit disable waits for resident shutdown
controller uninstall leaves no owned login entry and retains account choices
